rationale: Consolidate the duplicate LBJ Express and LBJ Infrastructure Group, LLC repository records under LBJ Infrastructure Group, LLC, the legal concession company, while preserving LBJ Express as the principal project alias. TxDOT and USDOT identify LBJ Infrastructure Group, LLC as the concession company and TIFIA borrower for the same IH 635 managed-lanes project marketed as LBJ Express, so the two published records represent one 52-year Dallas toll-road concession rather than separate portfolio companies. Correct APG's investment year from 2010 to 2012 because a federal P3 report states that APG joined in August 2012 by acquiring an interest from Meridiam. Ferrovial's audited 2025 ownership table and its SEC-filed May 2026 factbook confirm the current ownership split as Cintra 54.60%, LBJ Blocker (APG) 28.33%, and Meridiam Infrastructure S.a.r.l. (MI LBJ) 17.07%. Preserve APG Asset Management and Meridiam as separate active manager ownership periods with their disclosed stakes and vehicles, collapse only the explicitly mapped duplicate ownership and milestone rows, retain the unique 2025 anniversary milestone, deduplicate the sources, add the current project website, and retire the duplicate legal-name record through the canonical redirect workflow. Current Ferrovial, Meridiam, TxDOT, USDOT, and project materials show the concession in operation through 2061, and no later APG or Meridiam exit, pending sale, or change of control was found through August 8, 2026. Cintra's controlling interest is stated in the description and evidence but is not added as a manager ownership period because Cintra/Ferrovial is outside the supplied 100-manager census universe and no matching organization dependency exists in the approved task snapshot.

beforeImage.name: LBJ Express
beforeImage.description: LBJ Express is the trade name of the managed-lanes concession on I-635 and I-35E in Dallas County, Texas. Its users are commuters, freight carriers, and other motorists seeking priced travel-time reliability through the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex. The project operates under a long-term toll-concession structure with dynamic pricing, operations and maintenance obligations, and handback requirements at the end of the term. Public disclosures describe a roughly 13-mile corridor with six managed lanes and a total project cost of about $2.6 to $2.7 billion. The road fully opened in 2015 and has since become one of the larger managed-lanes projects in North America. The current project consortium is publicly described as including Cintra, Meridiam, and APG, while current ownership percentages are not publicly disclosed.

afterImage.name: LBJ Infrastructure Group, LLC
afterImage.description: LBJ Infrastructure Group, LLC is the concession company and TIFIA borrower for LBJ Express, a managed-lanes toll concession in Dallas County, Texas. Under a 52-year DBFOM comprehensive development agreement with the Texas Department of Transportation through 2061, the company financed, reconstructed, operates, and maintains approximately 13.25 miles of I-635 and I-35E, including dynamically priced managed lanes alongside rebuilt general-purpose and frontage roads. The project reached financial close in June 2010, began construction in January 2011, and fully opened in September 2015. Ferrovial's SEC-filed May 2026 factbook reports Cintra at 54.60%, APG at 28.33%, and Meridiam at 17.07%; Meridiam's current portfolio page identifies the corresponding non-Cintra vehicles as LBJ Blocker and MI LBJ.

milestones.event: TxDOT executed the 52-year comprehensive development agreement with LBJ Infrastructure Group, formerly LBJ Development Partners, for the IH 635 managed-lanes concession.
LBJ Infrastructure Group reached financial close for the LBJ Express concession one day after executing its $850 million TIFIA credit agreement.
Construction began on the LBJ Express managed-lanes project.
APG joined the LBJ Express concession by acquiring an ownership interest from Meridiam.
LBJ Express reached substantial completion with all lanes open to traffic.
Cintra, APG, and Meridiam acquired the Dallas Police and Fire Pension System's remaining LBJ interest; the resulting ownership was Cintra 54.60%, APG 28.33%, and Meridiam 17.07%.
The concession completed a refinancing that included approximately $615 million of tax-exempt private activity bonds replacing the original 2010 bonds.
The LBJ Express consortium marked ten years since the managed-lanes project opened to traffic.
